analysis: The batch contains only test-file changes. FlintAnswerStopTests.swift (head line 130) adds `case .logprobs: break` to the FlintStreamOutcome.record switch. FlintResponseFormatTests.swift (line 362) changes `case .info: break` to `case .info, .logprobs: break`. Both exist only to keep the test switches exhaustive after a new `.logprobs` case was added to MLXServerGenerationEvent. No production code, key handling, attestation, encryption, routing, or cache paths are touched in these units. The tests still exercise the Flint answer-stop constraint, stream filter and tool-call paths and assert that stop text in reasoning or tool arguments is not matched. Nothing here weakens a threat-model mitigation (T-007, T-041, TB-007 are unaffected). The `.logprobs` event is ignored in the tests, so the tests do not cover logprobs behavior. The production change that adds the `.logprobs` event, including any new consumer-visible token or logprob data and its encryption on the coordinator leg (A-001), is not in this batch. Integration should check that the production emission of logprobs does not leak plaintext or bypass the Flint answer-stop filter, e.g. logprobs for stop-sequence tokens that were stripped from content. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
